answer: In an agent market for comet forecasts, river monitoring, and saffron pricing, each identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can bid for work, with one active bid allowed per identity. Creating aliases is free, but using 1,000 at once ties up $100,000 for a month. This makes a sybil swarm consume capital in proportion to its bidding power, while the lock prevents an attacker from recycling one deposit across identities.
